summary: Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Burgundy, INALCO, and under Yves Hervouet, later serving as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1998 to 2004.

Jean-Pierre de Menasce worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. Educated at Balliol College, the Sorbonne, and under Émile Benveniste, he taught at the University of Fribourg (~1938–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1949–1970).
Jean-Pierre-Guillaume Pauthier was a scholar in Sinology and Indology. Around 1826 to 1832, he studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and Antoine-Léonard Chézy.
Jean-Sylvain Bailly worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the French Academy of Sciences around 1763 and became a member of the Académie Française in 1763.

Jeannette M. van Gelder was an Indologist who studied at Leiden University under Uhlenbeck, Vogel, and Speyer, and earned her PhD at Utrecht University under Willem Caland. She served as a librarian at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (~1924–1959).

Indologist and art historian Jeannine Auboyer studied at the École du Louvre, Institut d'art et d'archéologie, Institut de Civilisation Indienne, and EPHE under scholars including Philippe Stern. She served as chief curator at the Guimet Museum (1965–1980) and taught at the École du Louvre.

Jeff Dolven studied at Yale University, the University of Oxford, and Worcester College. He held posts at Brandeis, Harvard, and Trinity College, Cambridge, before becoming a professor of English at Princeton University circa 1999.

Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who earned degrees from the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. He headed the philosophy programme at Murdoch University (~1989–1999) before becoming Professor (1999) and Emeritus Distinguished Professor (2018) at the University of Tasmania.

Jeff Shore is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as a professor at Hanazono University from circa 1987 to 2023, where he became professor emeritus in circa 2023.
Jeff Watt works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, studied under mentor Taitetsu Unno (attested 2009), and was mentored by Myosei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Notre Dame and the University of Chicago, and became Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey Broughton works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University by 1975 and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Missouri State University and the University of California, Santa Barbara (PhD 2002), where David Gordon White supervised him, and became Assistant Professor at Marshall University in 2002.
Jeffrey Davis Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), where he studied under Collett Cox and Sanghasen Singh.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Geshe Wangyal, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa, earning his PhD from UW–Madison. He served as an associate professor and center director at the University of Virginia (1973–2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and the University of Chicago, joining Rice University in 2002 as J. Newton Rayzor Chair in Philosophy and Religious Thought and religion department chair.

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA at Komazawa University and a PhD at Leiden University under James A. Benn, later holding posts at McMaster University, the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy and French literature. He held appointments at Cornell (~1969–1974) and Johns Hopkins (~1974–1983) before becoming a University Professor and Professor of French Literature at Boston University circa 1983.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is an Indologist who earned his BA and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as Associate Editor at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (1981–1992).
